questions.q_en:
Which of the following examples for variations in the weather and climate of India is/are true?

I. While in the summer the mercury occasionally touches 55°C in the western Rajasthan, it drops down to as low as minus 45°C in winter around Leh.

II. In the Thar desert, if the day temperature is around 50°C, at night, it may drop down considerably up to 15°-20°C.
questions.solution_en:
· While in the summer the mercury occasionally touches 55°C in the western Rajasthan, it drops down to as low as minus 45°C in winter around Leh.

· Churu in Rajasthan may record a temperature of 50°C or more on a June day while the mercury hardly touches 19°C in Tawang (Arunachal Pradesh) on the same day.

· On a December night, temperature in Drass (Ladakh) may drop down to minus 45°C while Thiruvananthapuram or Chennai on the same night records 20°C or 22°C.

· These examples confirm that there are seasonal variations in temperature from place to place and from region to region in India.

· Not only this, if we take only a single place and record the temperature for just one day, variations are no less striking.

· In Kerala and in the Andaman Islands, the difference between day and night temperatures may be hardly seven or eight degree Celsius.

· But in the Thar desert, if the day temperature is around 50°C, at night, it may drop down considerably upto 15°-20°C.

questions.q_en: The Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) in July is located around:
options_en: South of the Tropic of Capricorn.
questions.solution_en:
In July, due to the apparent northward movement of the sun, the Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) shifts northward and is located around 20°N-25°N latitudes, over the Gangetic Plain in India.

The Inter Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ) is a low-pressure zone near the equator, where the northeast and southeast trade winds converge. It is characterized by rising warm air, heavy cloud formation, and frequent rainfall.

questions.q_en: The southwest monsoon enters the Kerala coast by approximately:
questions.solution_en:
The southwest monsoon typically enters the Kerala coast around June 1st, marking the onset of the monsoon season in India.

The Southwest Monsoon is a crucial weather phenomenon that brings heavy rainfall to India, especially during June to September.

Entry into India

· The monsoon winds originate from the Indian Ocean and are drawn towards the Indian subcontinent due to low-pressure formation over northwest India.

· The monsoon first hits the Kerala coast around June 1st, making Kerala the first state to receive monsoon rains.

· It then advances northward, covering the entire country by July.

questions.q_en: A break in the monsoon is characterized by:
options_en: Continuous heavy rainfall for several weeks.
A sudden and violent onset of rain.
Failure of rain to occur for one or more weeks during the southwest monsoon period.
The retreating of monsoon winds from the subcontinent.
questions.solution_en:
A break in the monsoon refers to a temporary dry period during the southwest monsoon season when rainfall stops for one or more weeks despite the season being active. This occurs due to factors like the shifting of the monsoon trough away from its normal position.

Causes of Monsoon Breaks

I. Northward shifting of the monsoon trough - The rain-bearing winds move away from the main landmass.

II. Strengthening of high-pressure systems over the Bay of Bengal.

III. Weakening of low-pressure systems over land.

These breaks can affect agriculture and water availability in India.

questions.q_en: Which of the following causes rainfall in northwestern India during winter?
options_en: Weak temperate cyclones from the Mediterranean Sea.

These temperate cyclones originate over the Mediterranean Sea and travel eastward, bringing light to moderate rainfall to the region.

This winter rainfall is important for the Rabi crops, especially wheat.

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the seasons in India and choose the correct option:

a. The cold weather season in north India is typically characterized by feeble high pressure conditions over the northern plain.

b. The hot weather season sees the ITCZ shift southward, leading to the prevalence of hot and dry 'Loo' winds in the northern plains.

c. The retreating monsoon season, occurring in October and November, is associated with clear skies and a rise in temperature, often referred to as 'October heat'.
questions.solution_en:
· During the cold weather season (winter) in north India, the region experiences feeble high-pressure conditions over the northern plains.

o This is because cold, dry air descends, creating stable conditions with light winds and low temperatures.

· The hot weather season (summer, March-May) sees the ITCZ shift northward, not southward.

o This northward shift creates low-pressure conditions over the northern plains, leading to the hot and dry 'Loo' winds.

· The retreating monsoon season (October-November) is marked by clear skies and a rise in temperature.

o This phenomenon is often called 'October Heat', as humidity remains high, leading to a temporary increase in temperature before winter sets in.

questions.q_en: The Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon causes very heavy rainfall on the:
options_en: Leeward side of the Western Ghats.
Windward side of the Sahyadris and Western Coastal Plain.
questions.solution_en:
· The Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon hits the Western Ghats (Sahyadris) first.

· The windward side (western slopes) of the Western Ghats and the coastal plain (Konkan & Malabar regions) receive very heavy rainfall due to orographic (relief) rainfall.

· As the monsoon winds rise along the slopes of the Western Ghats, they cool, condense, and cause heavy rainfall, especially in places like Mumbai, Goa, Mangalore, and Kerala.

questions.q_en: The Tamil Nadu coast remains relatively dry during the southwest monsoon season because:
options_en: It receives heavy rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch.
It is parallel to the Bay of Bengal branch of the southwest monsoon and lies in the rain-shadow area of the Arabian Sea branch.
The northeast monsoon is active during this period.
It experiences high temperatures and low humidity.
questions.solution_en:
The Tamil Nadu coast remains relatively dry during the southwest monsoon (June-September) because:

· The Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon flows parallel to the coast, reducing the chance of significant rainfall.

· The Western Ghats block the Arabian Sea branch, causing orographic rainfall on the windward side (Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra), leaving Tamil Nadu in the rain-shadow region.

questions.q_en: The average annual rainfall in India is about:
questions.solution_en:
The average annual rainfall in India is approximately 125 cm.

However, rainfall varies significantly across different regions:

· Areas of High Rainfall : The highest rainfall occurs along the west coast, on the Western Ghats, as well as in the sub-Himalayan areas is the northeast and the hills of Meghalaya. Here the rainfall exceeds 200 cm.

· Areas of Medium Rainfall : Rainfall between 100-200 cm is received in the southern parts of Gujarat, east Tamil Nadu, northeastern Peninsula covering Odisha, Jharkhand, Bihar, eastern Madhya Pradesh, northern Ganga plain along the sub-Himalayas and the Cachar Valley and Manipur.

· Areas of Low Rainfall : Western Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Jammu and Kashmir, eastern Rajasthan, Gujarat and Deccan Plateau receive rainfall between 50-100 cm.

· Areas of Inadequate Rainfall: Parts of the Peninsula, especially in Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and Maharashtra, Ladakh and most of western Rajasthan receive rainfall below 50 cm. Snowfall is restricted to the Himalayan.

o This rainfall is moderate to heavy, contributing significantly to agriculture in northern India.

questions.q_en: According to the Indian Meteorological Department, how many distinct seasons are found in India?
questions.solution_en:
The Indian Meteorological Department recognizes the following four seasons: the cold weather season, the hot weather or summer season, the southwest monsoon season, and the retreating monsoon season.

Winter (January - February)

· Cold and dry weather with low temperatures, especially in northern India.

· Influenced by Western Disturbances, bringing rain to northwest India.

Summer or Pre-Monsoon (March - May)

· High temperatures (above 40°C in some areas) and dry conditions.

· Hot winds like 'Loo' blow in the northern plains.

Southwest Monsoon or Rainy Season (June - September)

· Heavy rainfall due to the southwest monsoon winds.

· Orographic rainfall occurs along the Western Ghats and northeastern states.

Post-Monsoon or Retreating Monsoon (October - December)

· Monsoon winds withdraw, causing clear skies and rising temperatures (October Heat).

· The Northeast Monsoon brings rain to Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Odisha.

questions.q_en: Which of the following winds are described as 'displaced' equatorial easterlies?
questions.solution_en:
· The Southwest Monsoon winds are often referred to as "displaced equatorial easterlies" because they originate from the southeast trade winds of the Southern Hemisphere.

· Due to the Coriolis effect, these winds cross the equator and get deflected to the right, turning into southwesterly winds.

· These moisture-laden winds bring heavy rainfall to the Indian subcontinent during the monsoon season (June-September).

questions.q_en: The Bay of Bengal branch of the monsoon winds is deflected towards the Indian subcontinent by:
options_en: The high-pressure system over the Tibetan Plateau.
The Arakan Hills along the coast of Myanmar.
The low-pressure trough over North-West India.
questions.solution_en:
· The Bay of Bengal branch of the southwest monsoon originates from the Indian Ocean and moves northward.

· As these moisture-laden winds approach the coast of Myanmar, they encounter the Arakan Hills, which run parallel to the coast.

· The Arakan Hills deflect these winds toward the northeast, pushing them toward northeastern India, particularly Assam and Meghalaya.

· This results in heavy rainfall in places like Mawsynram and Cherrapunji, some of the wettest places on Earth.

· The remaining monsoon winds continue westward, bringing rainfall to Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and the Gangetic plains.
